summary: Bill M. Mak held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2017) and the University of Hamburg, where he was attested as a Research Fellow in 2026.

Bimal Krishna Matilal studied at the University of Calcutta, Sanskrit College and University, and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Quine and Føllesdal). He was Professor at the University of Toronto (~1968–1977) and Spalding Professor at Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha studied at Patna University and SOAS University of London (Ph.D. under Lionel David Barnett). He served as Head of Department at Patna University (1958) and Honorary Joint Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1968–1975).
Active in Buddhist and religious studies, Bing Chen held posts as Professor at Sichuan University (circa 1987) and at the Chengdu Academy of Social Sciences (attested 1993).
Bingtao Ma, working in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned an MA from Peking University (by 2008) and a PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2015).

Biraja Sankar Guha studied at Scottish Church College, the University of Calcutta, and Harvard University (AM 1920, PhD 1924). He served as Anthropologist at the Zoological Survey of India (1927) and Director of the Anthropological Survey of India (1945–1954).

Birgit Kellner earned her doctorate at Hiroshima University under Shoryu Katsura. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, she has held posts at Heidelberg University, the University of Vienna, and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Bisheshwar Nath Reu studied under Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha and worked in Indology and archaeology. He served at the Sumer Public Library (attested 1933) and headed the Government Museum Jodhpur and the Maharaja Man Singh Pustak Prakash Research Centre.
Biswajit Biswas, working in religious studies and Indology, studied under doctoral supervisor Rajat Kanti Das and was attested as a Research Scholar or Fellow at The Asiatic Society in 2026.
Biswanath Banerjee, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, was a faculty member at Visva-Bharati University from 1967 to 1991 and served as president of The Asiatic Society around 2003–2005.

Blain Auer works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He held a post as professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018) and served on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.
Bo Jiang works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Robert A. F. Thurman.

Bo Utas studied Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics at Uppsala University (~1958–1973) under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Stig Wikander. He subsequently held a post at Uppsala University from circa 1966 to 2003.
Bo-Kwang Han is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Dongguk University, where his post is attested in 2004 and 2015.
Bokar Rinpoche studied under traditional teacher Kalu Rinpoche from circa 1960 to 1989. A figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held a post at Bokar Monastery from circa 1984 until 2004.
Bong Seok Joo completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley and earned a PhD from Princeton University under Stephen F. Teiser. His academic fields are Buddhist studies and sinology.

Bongkil Chung earned his PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Florida International University in 1991–1992 and as professor of philosophy, attested in 2012.

Boris Turayev studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of St. Petersburg University (~1887–1891). He spent his academic career at Imperial St. Petersburg University (~1896–1914) and Saint Petersburg State University (~1914–1920) in history and archaeology.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1921–1925) and worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences from ~1926 to 1938.

Boris Vladimirtsov studied at St. Petersburg University (~1904–1908) and under Antoine Meillet (~1908–1909). Specializing in linguistics and Central Asian history, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts (~1915–1931) and the National Library of Russia (1924–1925).
